examples.title: Factorial
examples.description: A function with a local accumulator, a while loop and a return value.
examples.highlight: Two scopes in the symbol table: the globals, and factorial's locals.
examples.source:
# Implementing a Factorial Using NovaScript

define function factorial(n)
    let result be 1
    let i be 1

    repeat while i<=n
        set result to result*i
        set i to i+1
    end

    return result

end

let answer be call factorial(5)
say answer

examples.title: Fibonacci
examples.description: Ten Fibonacci numbers from an iterative three-variable swap.
examples.highlight: A void function — note the NONE return type inferred in the symbol table.
examples.source:
/*
Fibonacci sequence in NovaScript
*/

define function Fibonacci(n)
    let a be 0
    let b be 1
    let c be 0

    repeat while c<n
        say a
        let temp be b
        set b to a+b
        set a to temp
        set c to c+1
    end
end

call Fibonacci(10)

examples.title: Prime Sieve
examples.description: Every prime below 20, using integer division in place of modulo.
examples.highlight: A function called from inside a for-loop, with a nested while and a conditional.
examples.source:
# Print every prime number below 20.
# NovaScript has no modulo operator, so divisibility is
# tested with truncating integer division: (n/d)*d == n

define function isPrime(n)
    let d be 2
    let prime be 1

    repeat while d*d<=n
        when (n/d)*d==n then
            set prime to 0
        end
        set d to d+1
    end

    return prime
end

repeat for k from 2 to 20
    let p be call isPrime(k)
    when p==1 then
        say k
    end
end

examples.description: match / case dispatches on a value, inside a reusable function.
examples.highlight: The subject is evaluated once; each case body opens its own scope.
examples.source:
# Pattern matching in NovaScript.
# `match` evaluates its subject once, then runs the body of the first
# case whose pattern is equal to it. Each case body gets its own scope.

let day be 3

match day
    case 1 then
        say "Monday"
    case 2 then
        say "Tuesday"
    case 3 then
        say "Wednesday"
    case 4 then
        say "Thursday"
    case 5 then
        say "Friday"
end

examples.title: Exception Handling
examples.description: A division by zero is raised at runtime and caught by name.
examples.highlight: The catch variable is bound as a STRING in a fresh scope.
examples.source:
# Exception handling in NovaScript.
# The interpreter raises "Division by zero" at runtime and the
# catch block binds it to a string variable named `error`.

try
    let number be 0

    let result be 100 / number
    say result

catch error
    say "An error occurred: "
    say error
end

let count be 10

set count to "ten"
